newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds to see upside limited to 101.99.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds to see upside limited to 101.99.

text.p: LIFFE September Bund futures may have some limited upside potential but will then pull back on Tuesday, technical anlaysts said.

"There is potential for a near term push higher but I am really looking for either yesterday's high at 101.87 or 101.99, the previous high on February 27, to cap the market," said Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London.
At 0704 GMT September Bund futures were at 101.80, up nine basis points on the day. In early trade the contract had pushed just above 101.87 to a new contract high of 101.88.
Wilkin said from this region Bunds would correct lower.
"I'm looking for a pull back initially towards 101.28 which is a 50 percent retracement of the current rally from 100.69 to 101.87," said Wilkin.
He said there was an area of support between 101.28 and 101.22, the June 13 low.
"If we go down through 101.14, the 62 percent (Fibonacci) retracement, we would probably be looking for a deeper correction," he said.
Further out, Wilkin said the potential was for Bunds to pull back as low as 100.90, a 38 percent Fibonacci retracement of the main rally from 99.32, the May 29 low to 101.87, Monday's high.

"Daily studies are a little bit overbought but there is no real evidence of a short-term top forming yet and until I see that I wouldn't really want to call 100.90 yet, but underneath 101.14 there is that level," Wilkin said.
Miranda Churchill, an independant technical anlayst in London said a lot would depend on the glut of data out of the U.S. later in the session.
She said Bunds have the overall potential to reach 102.50 although not necessarily during this session.
"But the contract is very overbought, we are right through the top of the daily bollinger bands," she said.
"If the data is strong, there is a significant risk for a retracement. My long term view is still down," said Churchill.
She said the initial prop was at 101.56. That level was just above the May 14 and March 5 highs at 101.55.
A rejection of that would take Bunds down to an important support area around 101.24, Churchill said.
At the short end, September Euromarks were at 96.82, unchanged on the day, while December Euromarks were at 96.72, down one basis point.
